summary: The audit checks CSRE 100, two of CSRE 101A, 101B and 101C, NATIVEAM 100, a methodology course (3-5 units), a Community-Engaged Learning course (which may also count elsewhere), WIM and the capstone (CSRE 200X or 201X), and electives to reach 60 units: Native American Studies courses, with at most 8 units from other CCSRE programs, 5 units of Native language and 15 units of petitioned courses outside CCSRE. Required courses must be letter graded (unless offered only S/NC), and the core, methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a C- or better. Checked by hand: that no more than two classes are S/NC, and only as electives, and that at most 20 units are external credit. Honors is optional.

t6imtS9Y.why: "Native American Studies majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in Native American Studies" and "may count up to 8 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity (CSRE), or Jewish Studies (JEWISHST) courses". The 60 units are program.unitsMin, which counts every course the program's rules hold, so this pool takes the rest. Courses with a NATIVEAM listing never count against the 8-unit cap (many NATIVEAM courses are cross-listed in CSRE). Policies: "No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to electives in the Native American Studies major." CSRE 100 and the WIM, capstone and honors courses (CSRE 200X, 201X, 201Y, 201Z) count through their own requirements, so they are left out of the electives; otherwise the required capstone would use up the 8-unit allowance meant for elective courses.
